title: Dispatch: Sol review repairs batch A, combatant lifecycle (attempt 1)
description:
Repair batch A for the integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8: COMBATANT LIFECYCLE findings from the Sol review bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1` and read findings S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S11, S13 in full — each has a reproduced failure scenario). A parallel child (batch B) owns ammunition, rest, level-up, party, context, known limits, exhaustion helpers, and the audit report: DO NOT edit ammunition.ts, domainMutations.ts, rest.ts, levelUpEngine.ts, party.ts, contextAssembler.ts, ruleKnownLimits.ts, exhaustion.ts, exhaustionMutation.ts, ruleDispositions.ts, or their tests. Your files: state/encounterCombatants.ts, state/actionEconomy.ts, the combatant branches of orchestrator/toolRecordDeathSave.ts / toolStabilizeCharacter.ts / toolSetSuffocation.ts / toolUpdateCombatant.ts / toolBeginTurn.ts / toolStartEncounter.ts, and test/encounterCombatants.test.ts, test/actionEconomy.test.ts (or a new test file). No new migration (0036 is the last; use existing columns and campaign_actor.state_json).

SUPERVISOR DECISIONS (implement exactly):
S1 (damage at 0 HP): for a player-character combatant at 0 HP (dying or stable), damage whose magnitude is >= its effective hit point maximum (effectiveHpMax from state/exhaustion.ts — read-only import) is instant death; otherwise one failure (two if critical). Mirror hpLifecycle.ts applyDamage's character rule; share logic where practical.
S2 (suffocation counters): setCombatantSuffocation 'drop' preserves both death-save counters when the combatant is already dying; resets them only when entering dying from alive/stable/unconscious; clears any stable-recovery schedule when leaving stable. Mirror the character beginSuffocation.
S3 (terminal states): enforce on EVERY updateCombatant write, for both death-rule modes: (a) a combatant with exhaustion level 6 or with head_count 0 (multipleHeads mechanic) is dead and stays dead — any explicit status other than 'dead' or 'inactive' and any positive hpDelta is refused; (b) under player-character rules a dead combatant cannot be revived by status or healing (already partly done) and explicit 'escaped' / 'unconscious' / 'alive' on a dead combatant are refused ('inactive' — removal from the encounter — stays allowed). Monster-rules healing of a dead combatant keeps today's behavior except where (a) applies. The knockout exception (status 'stable' with damage from above 0 to 0 under PC rules) stays.
S4 (actor continuity): for identity_kind 'campaign_actor', the lifecycle facts that must survive encounters live in campaign_actor.state_json under one reserved key (e.g. "combatLifecycle": { deathRules, deathSaveSuccesses, deathSaveFailures, recoveryBlock, stableRecovery: {roll, anchor, deadline} | null, headCount }). syncCombatantActor and the updateCombatant actor sync write it atomically with the combatant row; startEncounter (and any other path that projects an existing campaign actor into a new combat instance) initializes the new row from it instead of from defaults/initialHeads. Preserve other state_json keys untouched. Validate the shape on read (malformed → refuse with a clear error, never silently default).
S5 (stale projections): when an actor is projected into a new encounter, transfer its pending stable-recovery schedule to the new row and null it on every older row of that actor (same transaction). resolveCombatantRecoveries resolves only the actor's current projection (the most recent row by combat instance start for that identity) and skips/clears superseded rows. record_death_save / stabilize_character / set_suffocation for a combatantId require the combatant's combat instance to be ACTIVE (as update_combatant already does); after combat ends, only the clock-driven recovery applies.
S11 (pre-0036 hydras): a combatant whose rules record carries the multipleHeads mechanic but whose head_count is NULL (encounter started before migration 0036) is unknown head state: updateCombatant damage/healing to it, begin_turn settlement for it, and reaction spends beyond the first are refused with an explicit error ("this combatant's head count is unknown because its encounter began before head tracking; close the combat instance and start it again"). Never treat NULL as one head silently. New encounters initialize as today.
S13 (head settlement): settle Multiple Heads at the end of the creature's own turn on every turn boundary, including when its turn is skipped or it is unavailable (dying, stable, unconscious, surprised) — find every path in beginTurn/actionEconomy that ends a participant's turn. When a recovery block is set (suffocating), commit the head regrowth and the boundary but suppress the HP gain (report 0 HP regained); never let a refused heal roll back the turn. Dead creatures never regrow.

TESTS (generalized, through the tool registry where model-facing): S1 matrix — dying/stable × critical/non-critical × damage below/equal/above effective max (incl. exhaustion 4); S2 — drop from alive, from dying with 1S/2F (preserved), from stable (schedule cleared), drop/breathe/drop sequence; S3 — exhaustion-6 PC combatant cannot be set alive or healed; hydra at 0 heads cannot be healed/revived; dead PC combatant refuses escaped/unconscious/alive, allows inactive; knockout still works; S4 — close/reopen continuity for a dying, a suffocating, and a stable actor, and a hydra with lost heads (state, then healing/death-save behaviour in the new encounter); S5 — the reproduced stale-recovery scenario (stabilize in C1, project into C2, die, advance past old deadline → actor stays dead) and lifecycle tools refused on a closed-instance id; S11 — a pre-0036-shaped hydra row (head_count NULL) refuses damage/settlement/extra reactions with the error; S13 — turn-end settlement for alive/unconscious/dying/dead, with recovery block and fire varied, asserting heads, HP gained, and that begin_turn succeeds.

Map every finding to its tests in your completion notes.
acceptance_criteria: All listed findings repaired with the listed tests; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report mapping findings to tests in bd notes; bead closed by the child.
